title: AI pillar — video 05 talking-point and screen rubric
note: Scored by gen-ceo-video-review.js --pillar ai. `judge_on: auto` criteria are measured by the deterministic probes in generators/lib/rubric-review.js and must not be supplied as verdicts. `screen` criteria are judged on the panels the deck embeds and need a `ref` (story#scN:panel.png). Evidence quoted only from an `also` story caps a narration verdict at partial. Keep ids stable: past verdicts bind to them.

scale.covered: Stated explicitly and clearly enough that a first-time viewer would take the point away.
scale.partial: Touched, implied, or named without enough substance to land — a viewer could miss it.
scale.missed: Not present in the narration at all.

weights.must: The video fails its job without this.
weights.should: Expected; its absence is a real gap worth fixing before the next cut.
weights.nice: Strengthens the story; acceptable to trade away for time.

dimensions.name: AI — agents on both sides of the trust line, with a human at every gate
dimensions.framing: The AI that builds and watches the governed estate, and the AI people use to consume it. Every AI action has an accountable human, every answer has a source, and preview is called preview.

criteria.name: Every scene shows a real tenant capture
criteria.expect: Each scene of the AI video embeds a qlik_panels/*.png captured from the live tenant. No drawn chart (QlikApp.app / barSvg), no missing file, no panel edited after capture.

criteria.name: A real AI surface is on screen
criteria.expect: At least one scene shows a real AI surface on the live tenant — an Answers response, an agent conversation, the Discovery or Insight agent configuration, or the coding agent's diff — rather than a generic panel reused from another story.
criteria.source: plan § F captures (Answers with citations, the Insight agent, automations with blocks)

criteria.name: Answers cite their sources
criteria.expect: An AI answer is shown citing its source document — the NinjaVan contract amendment behind the Singapore accuracy fall is the worked example — so the viewer sees it did not guess.

criteria.name: MCP exposes the governed tenant to any MCP client
criteria.expect: The Qlik MCP server exposes the governed tenant — data products, quality metrics, lineage, catalog — to any MCP-compatible assistant, not only Qlik's own, so this does not read as a closed vendor stack.

criteria.name: The insight agent has thresholds and a recipient
criteria.expect: The discovery/insight agent watches the governed products against stated thresholds — trust score below 0.7, sync lag over an hour, volume moving more than 50% — and its alert goes to a named recipient.

criteria.name: A human gate in front of every AI action
criteria.expect: Every AI action that changes data or reaches people has a named human gate — draft glossary terms await approval, low-confidence address repairs go to a steward, generated sheets and rules have an approver — on the consumption side as well as the build side.

criteria.name: Preview is said aloud
criteria.expect: The preview capabilities — the Qlik MCP server, declarative pipelines, sheet authoring over MCP — are called preview in the narration. On-screen small print does not count.

criteria.name: Where the model runs and where the data goes
criteria.expect: Data residency is stated: the language model can run in Meridian's own tenant, and customer data does not leave its infrastructure.

criteria.name: Trust is spent on the consumption side
criteria.expect: The build side produces trust and the consumption side spends it: the AI surfaces people use read the same governed products the build-side agents produced.

criteria.name: The coding-agent loop ends in a git revert
criteria.expect: A coding agent edits the pipeline YAML, the schema validates it, the human owns the decision, and a wrong change is a git revert.
